meta.after: In this freezing town, every tear you cry turns into a real glass key — the deeper the heartbreak, the bigger the key. Kids literally stub their toes just to unlock their lockers. Meanwhile, Bram chops onions in goggles to sell fake keys. Watch a pro! Boom, his shatters on a padlock. Fake tears freeze hollow. Me? Zero keys on my belt. Five years ago, Dad handed me his cracked watch and whispered, Be the strong one for Maya. I haven't cried since. Across the avenue, Frost Vault Door Nineteen guards the town's heat core behind a massive hex lock. Then a blizzard gust rips Dad's red scarf straight inside. It's the last thing we have of Dad! Maya dives in. Slam! The vault seals shut and the frost gauge plunges. Move, Stone-Face! Bram jams his onion key in. Snap! Useless dust. A neighbor kicks a crate for a pain tear. Crack! Way too tiny. Leo, I can't feel my fingers! Maya presses the frozen glass. Three seconds left. I clutch Dad's cracked watch. I'm sorry, Dad. Five years of grief finally break. A giant glowing Master Key freezes in my palms, shatters the ice seal, and swings Door Nineteen wide open. Maya crashes into my arms. One happy tear unlocks two hot cocoas — while Bram yells, Free cocoa, baby! and gets blasted into a snowbank.
